examples.en: There is a famous orchestra in our city.

examples.ko: 관현악단 연주회 표를 두 장 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two tickets for the orchestra concert.

examples.ko: 그 관현악단은 매년 해외 공연을 가요.
examples.en: That orchestra goes on overseas tours every year.
My younger sibling plays the violin in the school orchestra.
The orchestra and the choir went on stage together.
The conductor entered leading the orchestra.

explain: 현악기, 관악기, 타악기가 함께 연주하는 단체를 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '오케스트라'라고 많이 하고, '관현악단'은 공연 안내나 뉴스 같은 격식 있는 글에서 볼 수 있어요. '교향악단'도 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It means a group in which string, wind and percussion instruments play together. In daily talk people often say '오케스트라', while '관현악단' appears in concert notices and news, which are more formal. '교향악단' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: That athlete is an Olympic gold medalist.
A gold medalist came to our school and gave a talk.
I took a photo with a gold medalist.
I heard even gold medalists were ordinary kids at first.
A gold medalist's daily training is really long.

examples.ko: 이번 대회 금메달리스트에게 큰 박수를 보냈어요.
examples.en: We gave a big round of applause to this tournament's gold medalist.

explain: '금메달리스트'는 외래어 '메달리스트'에 '금'이 붙은 말이에요. 은메달은 '은메달리스트', 동메달은 '동메달리스트'로 이어서 써요. '금메달을 따다'로 말하고 '금메달을 받다'도 가능해요.
explain_en: 금메달리스트 is 금 plus the loanword 메달리스트. Silver and bronze follow the same pattern: 은메달리스트 and 동메달리스트. The usual verb is 금메달을 따다, and 금메달을 받다 also works.

examples.en: At first, that actor only played minor roles.
I appeared briefly in a drama as a bit player.
Even if it's a minor role, I want to act hard.
I heard my friend appeared in a movie in a small part.
Even the bit-part actors gather early at the set.
She started with minor roles and worked up to the lead.

explain: '주연', '조연'과 나란히 나오는 말인데, 단역은 대사가 거의 없거나 잠깐 나오는 역이에요. '단역 배우', '단역을 맡다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It sits alongside '주연' (lead) and '조연' (supporting), but a 단역 is a role with few or no lines or only a brief appearance. You say '단역 배우' or '단역을 맡다'.

examples.en: I go to learn pottery every weekend.
I made a cup myself in pottery class.
I became interested in pottery, so I signed up at a workshop.

examples.ko: 이 도예 작품은 색이 정말 독특해요.
examples.en: The color of this pottery piece is really unique.

examples.ko: 도예로 만든 그릇은 하나하나 모양이 달라요.
examples.en: Each bowl made by pottery has a different shape.
My friend gave me a pottery experience class as a gift.

explain: 만든 물건은 '도자기', 만드는 일이나 분야는 '도예'라고 해요. '도예 수업', '도예 공방', '도예 체험'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The finished item is '도자기' (ceramic ware), while the craft or field of making it is '도예'. It is often followed by another word, as in '도예 수업', '도예 공방' and '도예 체험'.

examples.en: That violinist is famous around the world.
My dream is to become a violinist.
The violinist slowly began to play on the stage.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 바이올리니스트의 공연을 보러 가요.
examples.en: This evening I'm going to see a violinist's performance.
The violinist next door practices every morning.
Young violinists entered the competition.

explain: 바이올린 연주자를 '바이올린 연주가'라고도 하지만 보통 '바이올리니스트'라고 해요. '피아니스트', '첼리스트'처럼 악기 이름 뒤에 '-니스트, -리스트'가 붙는 말이 많아요. 직업을 넓게 말할 때는 '연주자'예요.
explain_en: People also say 바이올린 연주가, but the usual word is 바이올리니스트. Many words follow the same pattern, like 피아니스트 and 첼리스트. For players in general the word is 연주자.

en: begin; get started in; take up

examples.en: I took up yoga last year.
I signed up at an academy to get into guitar.
More people are taking up golf.

examples.ko: 클라이밍에 입문한 지 두 달 됐어요.
examples.en: It's been two months since I started climbing.
I'm just about to start learning to cook.

examples.ko: 그림에 입문해서 매일 한 장씩 그려요.
examples.en: I got into drawing and draw one every day.

explain: 취미·운동·학문 앞에 '~에 입문하다'로 써요. '시작하다'보다 이제 막 그 세계에 들어선 느낌이 있어요. 책 제목의 '입문'은 처음 배우는 사람을 위한 책이라는 표시예요.
explain_en: It is used as '~에 입문하다' after a hobby, sport, or field. Compared with '시작하다' (start), it gives the feeling of having just stepped into that world. '입문' in a book title marks it as a book for beginners.

examples.en: Our teacher coaches our team.

examples.ko: 아버지가 어릴 때 제게 수영을 코치해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father coached me in swimming when I was little.

examples.ko: 면접 대답을 코치해 줄 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: I need someone to coach me on my interview answers.

examples.ko: 그는 십 년 동안 선수들을 코치했어요.
examples.en: He coached players for ten years.
I go to coach children in basketball every weekend.
I want to learn how to coach people.

explain: 일상에서는 '가르치다'가 더 흔하고, '코치하다'는 운동이나 면접처럼 기술을 옆에서 봐 주는 상황에 써요. 코치를 부를 때는 '코치님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily speech '가르치다' is more common; '코치하다' fits situations where someone guides your skill from beside you, like sports or interview practice. You address a coach as '코치님'.
